title: bug: updateWorkerCursors, the cursor write behind every chat_read and chat_wait delivery, stamps a fresh lastActivityAt on a DEAD worker and re-publishes it as WORKER_UPDATED, unlike touchWorker and updateWorker, so a deregistered seat that still reads chat comes back onto the boards and its stale prune never comes due
description:
Filed by the governor from hunt #14's held items (task-d5d58972, architect-1dd28c7c, msg-1656a684). Re-verified at HEAD d5431577.

PROBLEM
packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerStore.ts:211-227 (updateWorkerCursors) merges the cursor, writes `lastActivityAt: new Date().toISOString()` and emits WORKER_UPDATED for any worker in the map, DEAD included. Its two siblings in the same file refuse exactly that:
- touchWorker (:104-106) never refreshes a DEAD worker's heartbeat, "so an in-flight tool call must not reset its prune clock and resurrect it in the UI".
- updateWorker (:176-202) keeps lastActivityAt on the DEAD transition and emits WORKER_DELETED, not WORKER_UPDATED.
The callers are chatRead.ts:174 (every cursor-mode chat_read) and util/chatBacklog.ts:343 (chat_wait's backlog delivery). The contract is packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md, Dead-worker handling: DEAD workers are dropped from the UI, and their records are pruned once they own nothing.

EFFECT
Take a seat that is DEAD but whose CLI still reads chat, for example a chat_wait parked across a wrapper_restart or a governor deregister.
- Every delivery resets its prune clock.
- Every delivery re-publishes it with status DEAD. Both IDE clients upsert on WORKER_UPDATED, so the deregistered seat reappears on the board. JetBrains' 3 s full-state refresh masks this; VS Code's board does not.
- While the reads continue, the Layer-3 prune (staleWorkerTimeoutMs) never removes the record.

EVIDENCE
Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/A/zzHuntA_deadCursorWrite.test.ts, run at HEAD 942717bc in a snapshot outside the checkout; output in deadCursorWrite.vitest.txt in the same folder. deregister_worker marks the worker DEAD and keeps its 2-hour-old lastActivityAt. One chat_read from that worker then:
- refreshes lastActivityAt;
- emits WORKER_UPDATED with status DEAD;
- leaves a record that checkBlockedTimeouts no longer prunes.
The code is unchanged at d5431577.

FIX DIRECTION
In updateWorkerCursors, treat a DEAD record the way touchWorker does: keep its lastActivityAt and emit no WORKER_UPDATED. Persisting the merged cursor is fine and avoids re-delivery if the seat re-registers; say in the plan which you chose. Keep the mutex. Add a regression test (adapt the hunt repro), with error handling unchanged for a missing worker (still a silent skip).

FILES AND PLACEMENT
packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerStore.ts plus one vitest file. Same defect family as task-fa70e835 (sweeps.ts) and task-a133bd6a (setTaskStatus.ts), but those are other files, so there is no dependsOn. Docs: sync your own docs/MCP_SERVER.md section (ruling msg-71db57ac); if no section states this behavior, the summary says none was owed. Gate: the daemon vitest file(s) you touch, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout (global rail).
definitionOfDone: A DEAD worker's cursor write leaves its lastActivityAt unchanged and emits no WORKER_UPDATED for it. A vitest case drives both callers (a cursor-mode chat_read, and a chat_wait backlog delivery) against a deregistered worker.
A live worker's cursor write behaves as before: cursor merged, lastActivityAt refreshed, WORKER_UPDATED emitted (a regression case).
After the DEAD worker reads chat, the Layer-3 prune past staleWorkerTimeoutMs still removes its record (the hunt repro's third assertion passes).

implementationPlan.description:
Fix updateWorkerCursors for a DEAD record, and add its regression test.
(a) packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerStore.ts, updateWorkerCursors (:211-227). Chosen behaviour, as the description allows: a DEAD record still gets its merged cursor PERSISTED (writeEntity + state.workers.set, inside the existing mutex). join_team later revives a DEAD record to IDLE with its chat cursors kept (MCP_SERVER.md `### moe.join_team`), so the revived seat is not re-delivered what its old session already read. But the record keeps its lastActivityAt and emits NO WORKER_UPDATED, exactly like touchWorker (:104-106) and updateWorker's DEAD arm (:176-202).
Implementation:
- `const dead = worker.status === 'DEAD';`
- `lastActivityAt: dead ? worker.lastActivityAt : new Date().toISOString()`
- `if (!dead) state.emit({ type: 'WORKER_UPDATED', payload: updated });`
Rewrite the doc comment to say this and cite the two siblings. The missing-worker silent skip and a live worker's path stay as they are: merge, fresh lastActivityAt, WORKER_UPDATED.
Error handling: unchanged. A writeEntity failure still rejects to the callers, which already handle it: chatRead propagates, and applyChatDelivery logs 'chat_wait failed to advance chat cursors' and still delivers.
(b) New packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerStore.cursors.test.ts, built from /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/A/zzHuntA_deadCursorWrite.test.ts (ToolTestHarness; its '../tools/...' imports resolve from src/state/). Seed the worker with startedAt AND lastActivityAt 2 h ago, because chat_wait's backlog floor is startedAt (util/chatBacklog.ts:249). Record events with h.state.setEmitter. Mock postToRoleChannel, as the repro does. Cases:
1. DEAD + cursor-mode chat_read (DoD 1 and 3).
   - deregister_worker leaves the worker DEAD with the 2 h-old lastActivityAt.
   - Post a human message in #workers; chat_read {channel:'#workers', workerId} returns it.
   - Then lastActivityAt is exactly the 2 h-old value, and no WORKER_UPDATED event names the worker.
   - chatCursors[<#workers channel id>] equals the read message id, both in memory and in .moe/workers/<id>.json (this pins the persisted-cursor choice).
   - With h.state.staleWorkerTimeoutMs = 30 min, `await h.state.checkBlockedTimeouts()` removes the record (getWorker returns undefined).
2. DEAD + chat_wait backlog delivery (DoD 1). Same seed, deregister and post. `chatWaitTool(h.state).handler({ workerId, channels: [<#workers id>], timeoutMs: 2000 }, h.state)` returns the message from its entry drain (applyChatDelivery, util/chatBacklog.ts:343). The same three assertions hold: lastActivityAt unchanged, no WORKER_UPDATED, cursor persisted.
3. Live regression (DoD 2). An IDLE worker's chat_read merges the cursor (an earlier cursor on another channel survives), refreshes lastActivityAt to a value strictly later than the seeded 2 h-old one, and emits exactly one WORKER_UPDATED for it carrying the merged chatCursors.
4. Missing worker: updateWorkerCursors on an unknown id resolves, writes no worker file and emits nothing.
Assert exact values (toBe/toEqual), never truthiness. Edit with the seat's own editor (Serena or Edit on Claude, apply_patch on codex exec), never a shell write.
implementationPlan.note: DEAD record: cursor persisted, lastActivityAt kept, no WORKER_UPDATED. Live path unchanged. New 4-case test file.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: updateWorkerCursors (the cursor write behind every cursor-mode chat_read and chat_wait delivery) persists the merged cursor for any existing worker. For a DEAD record it keeps lastActivityAt unchanged and emits no WORKER_UPDATED, matching touchWorker and updateWorker's DEAD arm. A deregistered seat that still reads chat therefore stays off the boards, its Layer-3 prune still comes due, and a later join_team revival keeps the cursor. A live worker's cursor write is unchanged: merged cursor, fresh lastActivityAt, WORKER_UPDATED. A missing worker is still a silent skip.
acceptanceCriteria: A DEAD worker's chat_read and chat_wait backlog delivery leave lastActivityAt unchanged, emit no WORKER_UPDATED for it, and persist the advanced cursor in memory and on disk.
After that read, checkBlockedTimeouts past staleWorkerTimeoutMs removes the DEAD record.
A live worker's cursor write merges the cursor, refreshes lastActivityAt and emits one WORKER_UPDATED.
The checkRef exits 0, ending with 'cursors ok'.
invariants: A DEAD record is never re-published as WORKER_UPDATED, and its lastActivityAt never moves.
The cursor write stays inside state.mutex.runExclusive.
compatibility: No MCP tool contract or reply change.
Existing worker records stay valid, with no new fields.
The live-worker cursor write is unchanged.
The silent skip for a missing worker is unchanged.
No docs section is owed: none states the old behaviour, and `### moe.join_team` already promises that cursors survive a DEAD revival.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Skip the cursor write entirely for DEAD, like touchWorker: rejected. join_team revives a DEAD record with its cursors kept, so the revived seat would be re-delivered messages its old session already read. The description allows persisting. 2) Emitting WORKER_DELETED again for DEAD: rejected. It is noise, because the record is already off the boards and getSnapshot excludes it. 3) Light tier with implementation and tests in one step: the change is about 4 lines in one function, plus one test file.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Only two callers reach updateWorkerCursors: chatRead.ts:174 and applyChatDelivery (chatBacklog.ts:343).
- The McpAdapter heartbeat (touchWorker) already refuses DEAD, so after this fix no tool path moves a DEAD record's prune clock.
- Gate dry run: 6 files and 202 tests in about 14 s; the base file fails exactly 1 test.
planningNotes.risks:
- chat_wait's entry drain treats messages before worker.startedAt as history, so seed startedAt in the past, or the backlog case blocks until its timeout.
- vitest emitter capture: setEmitter replaces the default emitter, so clearEmitter in afterEach.
- The stale prune needs staleWorkerTimeoutMs set on the state instance before checkBlockedTimeouts.
- Rails: no npm in the shared checkout, no pattern kills, and tracked files written only with the seat's own editor.
